description: The machine crashes while the client downloads a package: the server sends half of the file and holds the rest; the runner kills the driver (2.6 to 3.5 s after it said it started), writes what a crash could have left of the state file, and starts it again on the same directory, the half-written file still there. The server holds only that first download: the client must download it again into a file of its own, never the one left behind, and install the whole file. The first run is killed late (8 to 11 s in) for the same reason as `restart-mid-download`'s is long: on a cold, busy ARC runner a Java client's first exchange has taken more than 3 s, and a kill before the download starts tests nothing.

offer.name: held
offer.content: a package the server sent half of before the crash
